info.name: QuickTweets — Verification (M1–M9)
info.description:
Manual verification of the Media subsystem and core flows before M10/M11.

IMPORTANT: Reference Coordination (the media_references ledger), TweetMedia rows, and MediaObject internals are NOT exposed by any API. This collection drives state; the DB checkpoints in verification-runbook.md verify coordination in pgAdmin. Run phase by phase, pausing at each checkpoint.

Auth: the access token is captured from the body into {{accessTokenA/B}} and sent as Bearer. The refresh + qt_session cookies are handled by Postman's cookie jar automatically. Because two users share one cookie jar on localhost, always authorize with the per-user Bearer token, never the cookie.

item.name: 00 · Health & Setup
item.description: Sanity check the server and DB ping before anything else.

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description: Register two users, log in, inspect /me, rotate refresh, and log out. Two users are mandatory for the cross-principal media tests later.

exec: pm.test("no avatar for a plain register", () => pm.expect(d.user.avatar).to.eql(null));
pm.test("no avatar for a plain register", () => pm.expect(d.user.avatar).to.eql(null));
// DB: every remaining refresh_tokens row for A is now gone. Register + Login
// created two sessions; Logout removed one, Logout-all removes the rest.

item.name: ✗ Failure paths
item.description: Deliberate failures. NOTE: authLimiter = 10 requests / 15 min on register+login — run these sparingly or expect 429s.

item.name: 02 · Media — primitives
item.description: The two upload paths (grant and Bearer), read, and the failure grid. A grant is single-use (GRANT_MAX_OBJECTS=1): mint one per grant-upload.

exec: pm.test("grant + expiry returned", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.grant).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(d.expiresAt).to.be.a("string"); });

item.name: Upload under Bearer (User A) → media token A1
✗ Failure paths
item.description: Upload and read failures.

item.name: 03 · Avatar (pre-auth adoption)
item.description: The register-with-avatar vertical: grant → upload → register{avatar}. DB CHECKPOINT after the happy path (see runbook §Avatar): a user-avatar:{id} ledger row must exist.

item.name: ✗ Failure paths
item.description: Adoption guards. These reuse the spent token/grant from the happy path above.

item.name: Token without a valid grant (not adoptable)

exec: pm.test("a leaked token alone is not adoptable (422)", () => pm.expect([422, 401]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: 04 · Tweets + media (M7–M9)
item.description: The heart of this phase. Every mutating step has a DB CHECKPOINT in the runbook (§Tweet coordination). Upload tweet media under Bearer (authenticated author) — no grant, no adoption.

item.name: Upload media B1 (Bearer B) — for cross-principal test
Edit — body only, omit media (media untouched)
Edit — reorder only [A2, A1] (should signal nothing)

exec: pm.test("still 2 media, order swapped", () => { const m = pm.response.json().data.media; pm.expect(m.length).to.eql(2); });

item.name: ✗ Failure paths
item.description: Attach-authorization and validation.

item.name: Create — cross-principal attach (A attaches B's object)

exec: pm.test("opaque — does not name the token", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include(pm.environment.get("mediaTokenB1")));

item.name: Create — duplicate media in one tweet
Delete — someone else's tweet (B deletes A's)
05 · Comments
item.description: Create/read/update/delete. Requires a live tweet — recreate one first if 04 deleted it.

item.name: Update — someone else's comment (B edits A's)
06 · Likes
item.description: Toggle like on/off. Uses the tweetId from 05.

item.name: 07 · Follows
item.description: B follows A, lists, then unfollows.

item.name: 08 · Comment Media
item.description: The third media producer (single file per comment) and its NEW path — the transitive cascade. Each lettered scenario is self-isolated: it mints its own media and its own comment, under a dedicated variable, so no scenario can leak state into another. DB checkpoints CM-1…CM-6 live in the runbook (§ Comment media checkpoints); the final invariant is Checkpoint F (extended for comments). Comment media is uploaded under Bearer (the authenticated author) — no grant, no adoption.

item.name: 0 · Setup (shared)
item.description: Run once before the lettered scenarios. Creates the host tweet the CRUD scenarios comment on, and uploads B's object for the cross-principal failure. Requires folder 01 to have set accessTokenA/accessTokenB.

item.name: S1 · Host tweet for comment CRUD

request.description: Produces {{cmTweetId}}. Reused (read-only) by scenarios A, B, C, D. Never mutated or deleted.
Produces {{cmMediaB}} — B's own object, used ONLY by scenario D (cross-principal).

item.name: A · Create with media
item.description: CMT-M01/M02. Prereq: Setup. Fresh media → comment-with-media on the host tweet → read it back. DB: Checkpoint CM-1.

request.description: Produces {{cmMediaCreate}} (fresh, this scenario only).
Consumes {{cmTweetId}}, {{cmMediaCreate}}. Produces {{cmCreateCommentId}}. → CHECKPOINT CM-1 in pgAdmin.
Consumes {{cmTweetId}}. Read-only; confirms the read path resolves the reference to a token.

exec: pm.test("a comment carries media", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.some(c => c.media && c.media.token)).to.be.true);

item.name: B · PATCH set / replace / remove
item.description: CMT-M03…M06. Prereq: Setup. Its OWN comment (starts with NO media) and its OWN two objects, so the set-difference is unambiguous. DB: Checkpoint CM-2 after each PATCH.

request.description: Produces {{cmPatchCommentId}}. Deliberately media-free so B4 exercises the none→set branch.
Produces {{cmMediaSet}}.
Produces {{cmMediaReplace}}.
none→set: begin only. → CHECKPOINT CM-2 (one row = set object).
set→replace: end set, begin replace. → CHECKPOINT CM-2 (one row = replace object; set object now unreferenced).
Same object resubmitted: neither end nor begin. → CHECKPOINT CM-2 (UNCHANGED — same single row).
replace→none: end only. → CHECKPOINT CM-2 (ZERO rows; replace object now unreferenced).

item.name: B8 · PATCH body only, media omitted

request.description: Omitted media leaves references untouched (here: still zero). Confirms omit ≠ null.

item.name: C · Delete with media
item.description: CMT-M07. Prereq: Setup. Its OWN fresh media + comment, held right up to deletion. DB: Checkpoint CM-3.

request.description: Produces {{cmMediaDelete}}.
Produces {{cmDeleteCommentId}} (carries {{cmMediaDelete}}).
Ends comment:{id}. → CHECKPOINT CM-3 (row gone; object survives unreferenced).

item.name: D · Cross-principal attach (failure)
item.description: CMT-M08. Prereq: Setup (owns {{cmMediaB}}). A tries to attach B's object → 422, opaque, rolled back. DB: Checkpoint CM-4.

request.description: Consumes {{cmMediaB}}. Expect 422; response must NOT name the token. → CHECKPOINT CM-4 (no stray comment / ledger row).

exec: pm.test("opaque — does not name the token", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include(pm.environment.get("cmMediaB")));

item.name: E · Transitive cascade (tweet delete)
item.description: CMT-M09 — the headline. A cascade tweet that carries its OWN media AND has a comment carrying its OWN media. Deleting the tweet must end tweet:{id} (via deleteWithMedia) AND comment:{id} (via deleteForTweet) in one transaction. DB: Checkpoint CM-5.

request.description: Produces {{cmCascadeTweetMedia}} — attached to the TWEET.

item.name: E2 · Create cascade tweet WITH media

request.description: Produces {{cmCascadeTweetId}} (carries {{cmCascadeTweetMedia}} → tweet:{id} ledger row).
Produces {{cmCascadeCommentMedia}} — attached to the COMMENT.

item.name: E4 · Comment WITH media on the cascade tweet

request.description: Produces {{cmCascadeCommentId}} (carries {{cmCascadeCommentMedia}} → comment:{id} ledger row).
One transaction: comment deleted, comment:{id} ended, tweet deleted, tweet:{id} ended. → CHECKPOINT CM-5 (both families ended; both objects survive unreferenced).

item.name: F · Restrict backstop (DB-only)
item.description: CMT-M10. The API path deletes comments first, so the comments→tweet FK never fires there. This sets up a tweet+comment; the raw DELETE proof runs in pgAdmin (Checkpoint CM-6) to confirm the ON DELETE RESTRICT backstop is real.

request.description: Produces {{cmRestrictTweetId}}.
Produces {{cmRestrictCommentId}}. Media-free so the ONLY thing that can block a raw tweet delete is comments_tweet_id_fkey. → CHECKPOINT CM-6 (raw DELETE refused).
